title: Data Classification and Storage Decisions Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies data classification and storage decisions?
options: Classify each field and minimise persistence before selecting location, encryption, backup, retention, and recovery controls.
Encrypt the entire cache with one immortal key
Store all fields in preferences for consistency
Assume internal storage needs no threat analysis
questions.answer: Classify each field and minimise persistence before selecting location, encryption, backup, retention, and recovery controls.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Encryption at rest prevents sensitive plaintext from ever appearing in process memory.
questions.explanation: Labelling all internal-storage data “secure” skips field sensitivity, integrity, backups, device compromise, sharing, retention, and recovery requirements.

questions.prompt: Which decision should precede choosing an encryption API?
questions.answer: Whether the value needs to be persisted at all, followed by its classification and lifecycle requirements.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
